Triggers include ovrcr, a new worktree workspace, terminal send, terminal keystroke, or an interactive agent session.

# OVRCR

Drive the installed `ovrcr` binary. One server owns every session. Every command names its project and workspace; the current directory is never a target.

In an interactive shell, leave `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET` unset unless the user chose an instance, resolve the binary once, and use the quoted `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE"` in every command below:

```sh
export OVRCR_EXECUTABLE="$(command -v ovrcr)"
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version
```

OVRCR Operator is different: `OVRCR_EXECUTABLE` is already set to the matching binary. Use it exactly as inherited; do not run that export, do not resolve a PATH-selected alternate, and do not fall back to a default instance. Preserve the inherited `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET`, and use only the exact project, workspace, session and run identities captured in the message. A `cargo run` from a checkout can speak a different protocol than the server that is already running. Pass `--json` on any command whose output you will parse. Run `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" <command> --help` for flags this page does not need.

The full contract is `docs/cli-reference.md` in the ovrcr source repository.

`automatic_local_terminals` is one global preference in `dashboard.toml`:

- `on` creates a `local` shell for every newly provisioned workspace.
- `off` skips automatic shells, including in the default-branch workspace.
- `default_branch_only` creates one only in the project's detected default-branch workspace. This is the default when no choice is saved.

Cycle and save it with Browse `L`, or edit `dashboard.toml`. The saved choice survives restart; the running server reads it on the next provisioning request. Changing it leaves existing terminals and agents untouched. Explicit terminal and agent launches work under every option.

## 1. Resolve the project

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project list --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project get NAME --json
```

Done when the JSON names the repo. Register a repository only when the user asked to add one:

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project add NAME /absolute/repo --workspace-root /absolute/worktrees
```

Registration creates the protected root workspace on the detected default branch. Whether it also starts a `local` shell follows `automatic_local_terminals` in `dashboard.toml` (default **default branch only**).

## 2. Create a workspace

A new branch needs `--base`. Read the repository's default branch and pass that name. An existing local branch uses `--branch` and takes no `--base`. The workspace's name is the branch, slashes included.

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --new-branch temp/topic --base DEFAULT --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --branch existing/branch --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace get --project NAME --branch temp/topic --json
```

Done when `workspace get` returns `path` and `branch`. Creation starts a separate `local` shell only when `automatic_local_terminals` is `on` (the default is **default branch only**, so feature workspaces do not get one automatically). Start a terminal explicitly with `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new` when you need a shell.

## 3. Open a terminal

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- /bin/sh
```

`terminal create` takes the same arguments. The program and its arguments go after `--`. With no program, OVRCR launches `$SHELL`. The JSON field `id` is the session id. Omit `--name` to let the title follow the app.

Done when `terminal list --json` shows that id with `phase` `running`.

## 4. Start an interactive agent

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- \
  "$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run PROVIDER -- "$(command -v BIN)"
```

`PROVIDER` is `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, or `omp`. `BIN` is that provider's executable. Pass the absolute binaries from `command -v`; the server runs this argv.

Managed Claude, Codex, Pi, and Oh My Pi launches auto-trust by default. When the argv has no permission-mode, approve, auto-approve, full-auto, or dangerously-* flag, `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run` adds one:

- Claude: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (not `--permission-mode dontAsk`)
- Codex: `--full-auto`
- Pi: `--approve`
- Oh My Pi: `--auto-approve`

A flag already in that family wins: it is not appended to or replaced. There is no global switch. Grok, Hermes, and Cursor are not given one. Omit the trust flag in the command below; the managed launch adds Claude's.

A Claude Code launch through this route was exercised end to end, including a prompt sent after the composer appeared. Omit permission flags so the managed launch adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions`:

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- \
  "$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run claude -- "$(command -v claude)"
```

Flags that keep a fresh Claude launch eligible for reporting: `--model`, `--permission-mode`, `--agent`, `--agents`, `--settings`, `--setting-sources`, `--system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--name` / `-n`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--verbose`, and permission-bypass flags, including the default `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. A fresh launch may take one prompt after a second `--`.

`--print` / `-p` is the one-shot mode. It prints, exits, and the screen reports `agent admission unavailable`. An interactive session stays at the composer.

Done when `terminal read ID` shows the composer. Claude's composer is the `❯` prompt. A trust dialog or other menu is not done. Paste cannot move a menu selection. Answer a menu with Keystrokes only when the user asked for that answer (see below); otherwise stop and show the user that screen.

## 5. Send a prompt

Send only after the composer is on screen:

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal send ID --text 'Reply with exactly these two words and nothing else: hello world. Do not use tools.'
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal read ID --max-lines 40
```

That is how a prompt is submitted. Arrow keys and other control sequences are text in that paste, so this command is for a line the program should receive, then Enter.

Done when the reply is visible, or when you stop because the screen is a menu, the session has exited, or the composer is still waiting with no reply. Show that screen.

```sh

"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal keystroke ID :enter:
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal read ID --max-lines 40
```

```sh

"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace remove --project NAME --branch BRANCH
```

- `protocol version mismatch`: the binary and the running server differ. Report the versions. Restart the server only when the user asked. `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" shutdown --kill` stops their live sessions.
- `agent admission unavailable`: relaunch through `agent run` without print mode or flags outside the eligible set. The interactive composer is the session to keep.

---
name: ovrcr-coordinator
description: Coordinate parallel coding or research through visible OVRCR Workspace Agent sessions, register watches, and verify asynchronous results.
---

# Coordinate OVRCR sessions

Use this workflow for work that needs multiple Workspace Agent sessions. For a
quick inspection or one small step, use Operator's CLI directly.

## Requirements

Operator supplies the OVRCR CLI and the `watch_sessions` tool. Run instance
commands as `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json ...`; the inherited instance and socket
select the user's live OVRCR Server. Verify command output and honor refusals.

## Installation

This skill is bundled with OVRCR and loaded explicitly for Operator. No project
or personal skill installation is needed. Check the available CLI with
`"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version` and `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --help`.

## Usage

### Dispatch work

1. Choose the route. Use Operator's Bash for a quick, single-step CLI task.
   For parallel coding, put each independent task in its own Git worktree
   Workspace on a dedicated branch. The Root workspace is protected; do not use
   it for delegated edits. Share a Workspace only for read-only research or
   when the user explicitly requests concurrent work on the same branch.
2. Reuse suitable running Retained sessions or create Agent sessions in those
   Workspaces. A typical worktree command is
   `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json workspace create --project PROJECT --new-branch BRANCH --base BASE`.
   Start a managed Agent with `terminal create` and `ovrcr agent run PROVIDER --`
   around its native executable, or use the Dashboard Agent picker. Do not
   assume a shell placeholder is an Agent session.
3. Before sending each task, read `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal list --json`.
   Match the intended session by its id and Workspace. Require `scope ==
   "Workspace"`, a valid `kind.agent`, and `phase == "running"`. If setup,
   trust, or approval input is unexpected, stop and ask the user; do not guess
   keystrokes.
4. Save the session's pre-send baseline: numeric `run`, numeric
   `agent.activity_revision`, and `unread.turn` exactly as returned (an opaque
   string or `null`). Do not parse or increment the unread turn. Pass it to
   `watch_sessions` as `baseline: {run, activity_revision, unread_turn}`; the
   tool's `unread_turn` field maps to CLI `unread.turn`.

   ```json
   {"action":"add","sessions":[{"session_id":42,"project":"example","label":"agent","baseline":{"run":7,"activity_revision":12,"unread_turn":null}}]}
   ```
5. Send each task with `terminal send SESSION_ID --text MESSAGE` (Paste). Ask
   for a final trailer in this form:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_DONE
   summary: what changed
   files: paths changed
   checks: command and exit code, or none requested
   ```

   If blocked, ask for:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_BLOCKED
   reason: the concrete blocker
   need: the information or decision required
   ```

6. After sending, call `watch_sessions` with `action: "add"` for every task,
   using the captured session id, project, label, and baseline. Then return a
   compact Task / Workspace / Session table and finish the turn immediately.
   Do not wait or poll in a shell; watched sessions keep Operator leased and
   the composer available for follow-up messages. Use `list` to report watches
   or `remove` when the user asks to stop watching. Removing a watch does not
   stop its Workspace session.

### Handle wakeups

On `AsyncWakeup`, use the reported session ids and current `terminal list
--json` rows to choose a provider read path:

- Claude Code and Codex: `terminal transcript SESSION_ID --json`. If a transcript
  entry is truncated at the 16 KiB cap, read the terminal tail with
  `terminal read SESSION_ID --max-lines N`.
- Pi and Oh My Pi: `terminal read SESSION_ID` or `terminal screen SESSION_ID`.

Read the full relevant reply once. If it omits the trailer, summarize what it
actually says and note that the marker was absent; do not resend the task just
to obtain formatting. A routine factual blocker can be answered within the
user's existing scope: capture a fresh baseline, use `terminal send`, then
register that session with `watch_sessions` again. Escalate human decisions and
`waiting_input` prompts as a concise question that identifies the session.

For coding tasks, work in the matching Workspace and verify `git status
--short --branch`, `git diff --stat`, and each reported check's actual exit
code before calling the result ready for review. A Ready observation or a
`OVRCR_WORKER_DONE` trailer alone does not prove success. Leave finished
Retained sessions open in the Dashboard unless the user asks to close or
archive them.

## Troubleshooting

If `watch_sessions` rejects a session for missing Reporter lifecycle data,
report that the session cannot be watched and use a managed Agent launch when
the user wants to continue. Do not infer completion from terminal silence or
switch that session to read-only polling.

# OVRCR

Drive the installed `ovrcr` binary. One server owns every session. Every command names its project and workspace; the current directory is never a target.

In an interactive shell, leave `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET` unset unless the user chose an instance, resolve the binary once, and use the quoted `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE"` in every command below:

```sh
export OVRCR_EXECUTABLE="$(command -v ovrcr)"
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version
```

OVRCR Operator is different: `OVRCR_EXECUTABLE` is already set to the matching binary. Use it exactly as inherited; do not run that export, do not resolve a PATH-selected alternate, and do not fall back to a default instance. Preserve the inherited `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET`, and use only the exact project, workspace, session and run identities captured in the message. A `cargo run` from a checkout can speak a different protocol than the server that is already running. Pass `--json` on any command whose output you will parse. Run `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" <command> --help` for flags this page does not need.

The full contract is `docs/cli-reference.md` in the ovrcr source repository.

`automatic_local_terminals` is one global preference in `dashboard.toml`:

- `on` creates a `local` shell for every newly provisioned workspace.
- `off` skips automatic shells, including in the default-branch workspace.
- `default_branch_only` creates one only in the project's detected default-branch workspace. This is the default when no choice is saved.

Cycle and save it with Browse `L`, or edit `dashboard.toml`. The saved choice survives restart; the running server reads it on the next provisioning request. Changing it leaves existing terminals and agents untouched. Explicit terminal and agent launches work under every option.

## 1. Resolve the project

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project list --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project get NAME --json
```

Done when the JSON names the repo. Register a repository only when the user asked to add one:

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project add NAME /absolute/repo --workspace-root /absolute/worktrees
```

Registration creates the protected root workspace on the detected default branch. Whether it also starts a `local` shell follows `automatic_local_terminals` in `dashboard.toml` (default **default branch only**).

## 2. Create a workspace

A new branch needs `--base`. Read the repository's default branch and pass that name. An existing local branch uses `--branch` and takes no `--base`. The workspace's name is the branch, slashes included.

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --new-branch temp/topic --base DEFAULT --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --branch existing/branch --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace get --project NAME --branch temp/topic --json
```

Done when `workspace get` returns `path` and `branch`. Creation starts a separate `local` shell only when `automatic_local_terminals` is `on` (the default is **default branch only**, so feature workspaces do not get one automatically). Start a terminal explicitly with `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new` when you need a shell.

## 3. Open a terminal

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- /bin/sh
```

`terminal create` takes the same arguments. The program and its arguments go after `--`. With no program, OVRCR launches `$SHELL`. The JSON field `id` is the session id. Omit `--name` to let the title follow the app.

Done when `terminal list --json` shows that id with `phase` `running`.

## 4. Start an interactive agent

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- \
  "$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run PROVIDER -- "$(command -v BIN)"
```

name: ovrcr-coordinator
description: Coordinate parallel coding or research through visible OVRCR Workspace Agent sessions, register watches, and verify asynchronous results.
---

# Coordinate OVRCR sessions

Use this workflow for work that needs multiple Workspace Agent sessions. For a
quick inspection or one small step, use Operator's CLI directly.

## Requirements

Operator supplies the OVRCR CLI and the `watch_sessions` tool. Run instance
commands as `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json ...`; the inherited instance and socket
select the user's live OVRCR Server. Verify command output and honor refusals.

## Installation

This skill is bundled with OVRCR and loaded explicitly for Operator. No project
or personal skill installation is needed. Check the available CLI with
`"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version` and `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --help`.

## Usage

### Dispatch work

1. Choose the route. Use Operator's Bash for a quick, single-step CLI task.
   For parallel coding, put each independent task in its own Git worktree
   Workspace on a dedicated branch. The Root workspace is protected; do not use
   it for delegated edits. Share a Workspace only for read-only research or
   when the user explicitly requests concurrent work on the same branch.
2. Reuse suitable running Retained sessions or create Agent sessions in those
   Workspaces. A typical worktree command is
   `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json workspace create --project PROJECT --new-branch BRANCH --base BASE`.
   Start a managed Agent with `terminal create` and `ovrcr agent run PROVIDER --`
   around its native executable, or use the Dashboard Agent picker. Do not
   assume a shell placeholder is an Agent session.
3. Before sending each task, read `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal list --json`.
   Match the intended session by its id and Workspace. Require `scope ==
   "Workspace"`, a valid `kind.agent`, and `phase == "running"`. If setup,
   trust, or approval input is unexpected, stop and ask the user; do not guess
   keystrokes.
4. Save the session's pre-send baseline: numeric `run`, numeric
   `agent.activity_revision`, and `unread.turn` exactly as returned (an opaque
   string or `null`). Do not parse or increment the unread turn. Pass it to
   `watch_sessions` as `baseline: {run, activity_revision, unread_turn}`; the
   tool's `unread_turn` field maps to CLI `unread.turn`.

   ```json
   {"action":"add","sessions":[{"session_id":42,"project":"example","label":"agent","baseline":{"run":7,"activity_revision":12,"unread_turn":null}}]}
   ```
5. Send each task with `terminal send SESSION_ID --text MESSAGE` (Paste). Ask
   for a final trailer in this form:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_DONE
   summary: what changed
   files: paths changed
   checks: command and exit code, or none requested
   ```

   If blocked, ask for:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_BLOCKED
   reason: the concrete blocker
   need: the information or decision required
   ```

6. After sending, call `watch_sessions` with `action: "add"` for every task,
   using the captured session id, project, label, and baseline. Then return a
   compact Task / Workspace / Session table and finish the turn immediately.
   Do not wait or poll in a shell; watched sessions keep Operator leased and
   the composer available for follow-up messages. Use `list` to report watches
   or `remove` when the user asks to stop watching. Removing a watch does not
   stop its Workspace session.

### Handle wakeups

On `AsyncWakeup`, use the reported session ids and current `terminal list
--json` rows to choose a provider read path:

- Claude Code and Codex: `terminal transcript SESSION_ID --json`. If a transcript
  entry is truncated at the 16 KiB cap, read the terminal tail with
  `terminal read SESSION_ID --max-lines N`.
- Pi and Oh My Pi: `terminal read SESSION_ID` or `terminal screen SESSION_ID`.

Read the full relevant reply once. If it omits the trailer, summarize what it
actually says and note that the marker was absent; do not resend the task just
to obtain formatting. A routine factual blocker can be answered within the
user's existing scope: capture a fresh baseline, use `terminal send`, then
register that session with `watch_sessions` again. Escalate human decisions and
`waiting_input` prompts as a concise question that identifies the session.

For coding tasks, work in the matching Workspace and verify `git status
--short --branch`, `git diff --stat`, and each reported check's actual exit
code before calling the result ready for review. A Ready observation or a
`OVRCR_WORKER_DONE` trailer alone does not prove success. Leave finished
Retained sessions open in the Dashboard unless the user asks to close or
archive them.

## Troubleshooting

If `watch_sessions` rejects a session for missing Reporter lifecycle data,
report that the session cannot be watched and use a managed Agent launch when
the user wants to continue. Do not infer completion from terminal silence or
switch that session to read-only polling.

# Coordinate OVRCR sessions

Use this workflow for work that needs multiple Workspace Agent sessions. For a
quick inspection or one small step, use Operator's CLI directly.

## Requirements

Operator supplies the OVRCR CLI and the `watch_sessions` tool. Run instance
commands as `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json ...`; the inherited instance and socket
select the user's live OVRCR Server. Verify command output and honor refusals.

## Installation

This skill is bundled with OVRCR and loaded explicitly for Operator. No project
or personal skill installation is needed. Check the available CLI with
`"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version` and `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --help`.

## Usage

### Dispatch work

1. Choose the route. Use Operator's Bash for a quick, single-step CLI task.
   For parallel coding, put each independent task in its own Git worktree
   Workspace on a dedicated branch. The Root workspace is protected; do not use
   it for delegated edits. Share a Workspace only for read-only research or
   when the user explicitly requests concurrent work on the same branch.
2. Reuse suitable running Retained sessions or create Agent sessions in those
   Workspaces. A typical worktree command is
   `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --json workspace create --project PROJECT --new-branch BRANCH --base BASE`.
   Start a managed Agent with `terminal create` and `ovrcr agent run PROVIDER --`
   around its native executable, or use the Dashboard Agent picker. Do not
   assume a shell placeholder is an Agent session.
3. Before sending each task, read `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal list --json`.
   Match the intended session by its id and Workspace. Require `scope ==
   "Workspace"`, a valid `kind.agent`, and `phase == "running"`. If setup,
   trust, or approval input is unexpected, stop and ask the user; do not guess
   keystrokes.
4. Save the session's pre-send baseline: numeric `run`, numeric
   `agent.activity_revision`, and `unread.turn` exactly as returned (an opaque
   string or `null`). Do not parse or increment the unread turn. Pass it to
   `watch_sessions` as `baseline: {run, activity_revision, unread_turn}`; the
   tool's `unread_turn` field maps to CLI `unread.turn`.

   ```json
   {"action":"add","sessions":[{"session_id":42,"project":"example","label":"agent","baseline":{"run":7,"activity_revision":12,"unread_turn":null}}]}
   ```
5. Send each task with `terminal send SESSION_ID --text MESSAGE` (Paste). Ask
   for a final trailer in this form:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_DONE
   summary: what changed
   files: paths changed
   checks: command and exit code, or none requested
   ```

   If blocked, ask for:

   ```text
   OVRCR_WORKER_BLOCKED
   reason: the concrete blocker
   need: the information or decision required
   ```

6. After sending, call `watch_sessions` with `action: "add"` for every task,
   using the captured session id, project, label, and baseline. Then return a
   compact Task / Workspace / Session table and finish the turn immediately.
   Do not wait or poll in a shell; watched sessions keep Operator leased and
   the composer available for follow-up messages. Use `list` to report watches
   or `remove` when the user asks to stop watching. Removing a watch does not
   stop its Workspace session.

### Handle wakeups

On `AsyncWakeup`, use the reported session ids and current `terminal list
--json` rows to choose a provider read path:

- Claude Code and Codex: `terminal transcript SESSION_ID --json`. If a transcript
  entry is truncated at the 16 KiB cap, read the terminal tail with
  `terminal read SESSION_ID --max-lines N`.
- Pi and Oh My Pi: `terminal read SESSION_ID` or `terminal screen SESSION_ID`.

Read the full relevant reply once. If it omits the trailer, summarize what it
actually says and note that the marker was absent; do not resend the task just
to obtain formatting. A routine factual blocker can be answered within the
user's existing scope: capture a fresh baseline, use `terminal send`, then
register that session with `watch_sessions` again. Escalate human decisions and
`waiting_input` prompts as a concise question that identifies the session.

For coding tasks, work in the matching Workspace and verify `git status
--short --branch`, `git diff --stat`, and each reported check's actual exit
code before calling the result ready for review. A Ready observation or a
`OVRCR_WORKER_DONE` trailer alone does not prove success. Leave finished
Retained sessions open in the Dashboard unless the user asks to close or
archive them.

## Troubleshooting

If `watch_sessions` rejects a session for missing Reporter lifecycle data,
report that the session cannot be watched and use a managed Agent launch when
the user wants to continue. Do not infer completion from terminal silence or
switch that session to read-only polling.

# OVRCR

Drive the installed `ovrcr` binary. One server owns every session. Every command names its project and workspace; the current directory is never a target.

In an interactive shell, leave `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET` unset unless the user chose an instance, resolve the binary once, and use the quoted `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE"` in every command below:

```sh

"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" --version
```

OVRCR Operator is different: `OVRCR_EXECUTABLE` is already set to the matching binary. Use it exactly as inherited; do not run that export, do not resolve a PATH-selected alternate, and do not fall back to a default instance. Preserve the inherited `OVRCR_HOME`, `OVRCR_CONFIG` and `OVRCR_SOCKET`, and use only the exact project, workspace, session and run identities captured in the message. A `cargo run` from a checkout can speak a different protocol than the server that is already running. Pass `--json` on any command whose output you will parse. Run `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" <command> --help` for flags this page does not need.

The full contract is `docs/cli-reference.md` in the ovrcr source repository.

`automatic_local_terminals` is one global preference in `dashboard.toml`:

- `on` creates a `local` shell for every newly provisioned workspace.
- `off` skips automatic shells, including in the default-branch workspace.
- `default_branch_only` creates one only in the project's detected default-branch workspace. This is the default when no choice is saved.

Cycle and save it with Browse `L`, or edit `dashboard.toml`. The saved choice survives restart; the running server reads it on the next provisioning request. Changing it leaves existing terminals and agents untouched. Explicit terminal and agent launches work under every option.

## 1. Resolve the project

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project list --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project get NAME --json
```

Done when the JSON names the repo. Register a repository only when the user asked to add one:

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" project add NAME /absolute/repo --workspace-root /absolute/worktrees
```

Registration creates the protected root workspace on the detected default branch. Whether it also starts a `local` shell follows `automatic_local_terminals` in `dashboard.toml` (default **default branch only**).

## 2. Create a workspace

A new branch needs `--base`. Read the repository's default branch and pass that name. An existing local branch uses `--branch` and takes no `--base`. The workspace's name is the branch, slashes included.

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --new-branch temp/topic --base DEFAULT --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace create --project NAME --branch existing/branch --json
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" workspace get --project NAME --branch temp/topic --json
```

Done when `workspace get` returns `path` and `branch`. Creation starts a separate `local` shell only when `automatic_local_terminals` is `on` (the default is **default branch only**, so feature workspaces do not get one automatically). Start a terminal explicitly with `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new` when you need a shell.

## 3. Open a terminal

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- /bin/sh
```

`terminal create` takes the same arguments. The program and its arguments go after `--`. With no program, OVRCR launches `$SHELL`. The JSON field `id` is the session id. Omit `--name` to let the title follow the app.

Done when `terminal list --json` shows that id with `phase` `running`.

## 4. Start an interactive agent

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" new --project NAME --workspace BRANCH --name LABEL --json -- \
  "$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run PROVIDER -- "$(command -v BIN)"
```

`PROVIDER` is `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, or `omp`. `BIN` is that provider's executable. Pass the absolute binaries from `command -v`; the server runs this argv.

Managed Claude, Codex, Pi, and Oh My Pi launches auto-trust by default. When the argv has no permission-mode, approve, auto-approve, full-auto, or dangerously-* flag, `"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run` adds one:

- Claude: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (not `--permission-mode dontAsk`)
- Codex: `--full-auto`
- Pi: `--approve`
- Oh My Pi: `--auto-approve`

A flag already in that family wins: it is not appended to or replaced. There is no global switch. Grok, Hermes, and Cursor are not given one. Omit the trust flag in the command below; the managed launch adds Claude's.

A Claude Code launch through this route was exercised end to end, including a prompt sent after the composer appeared. Omit permission flags so the managed launch adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions`:

  "$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" agent run claude -- "$(command -v claude)"
```

A fresh launch may take one prompt after a second `--`.

`--print` / `-p` is the one-shot mode. It prints, exits, and the screen reports `agent admission unavailable`. An interactive session stays at the composer.

```sh
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal send ID --text 'Reply with exactly these two words and nothing else: hello world. Do not use tools.'
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal read ID --max-lines 40
```

Send writes the text, then Enter. `--no-submit` omits Enter. When the program has asked for bracketed paste, the text is pasted and Enter is written after the paste. That is how a prompt is submitted. Arrow keys and other control sequences are text in that paste, so this command is for a line the program should receive, then Enter.

`{"ok":true}` means the bytes were written. Read the screen again for the assistant's reply. The reply is the line after the echoed prompt. In the Claude run above, the screen showed the prompt and then `hello world`, with `phase` still `running` and `activity` `idle`.

## Press a key

`terminal keystroke` writes one key, as the keyboard would. It is never a paste:

```sh

"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal keystroke ID :enter:
"$OVRCR_EXECUTABLE" terminal read ID --max-lines 40
```

`:j:` then `:enter:` approves a menu that opens with No highlighted. A new workspace and its `local` shell stay up. Close a terminal, remove a workspace, or shut the server down only when the user asked. Live sessions and a dirty worktree block `workspace remove`. The root workspace cannot be removed.
